evidence.field: PDF p. 423, printed p. 411; 工部, 工 gōng headword and etymology paragraph. Scan: /home/catalin/hanzi-etymology-books/research-ocr/ziyuan-full/page-0423/source.png; source_pixel_sha256 5612d68e138d947d28c0a103b43738ef8d1f3e96f8af91b39dabadbbe2ba0b48
evidence.text: The paragraph identifies 工 as a pictograph resembling a carpenter’s square used to draw right angles or squares. It says an early end-frame contracted to a horizontal stroke by late Shang, while earlier Western Zhou bronze forms retained a thick lower stroke. The author proposes 矩 (a carpenter’s square) as the original referent, then presents craft worker as an early extension, with further extensions to skill and engineering; it traces 功績 from engineering and official/administrative senses from craft or engineering. These are this author’s proposed graphic and semantic account, not an independently established chronology. The page also cites the Western Zhou 伊簋 and the Analects for craft-worker senses, and reports a Western Zhou 金文 title written as an unresolved glyph followed by 工, conventionally written 司空 in transmitted texts.
evidence.title: 字源, 2012 edition (catalogue record search; used only for publication metadata)

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫, Chinese University of Hong Kong
evidence.field: 工 character entry, graph analysis and examples
evidence.text: The database reports competing interpretations of the early graph: a bladed tool whose upper part may have served as a carpenter’s square (attributed to 季旭昇), a square (attributed to 楊樹達), or a building tool (attributed to 鄒景衡 and 劉新民). It reports oracle-bone examples as a state/place name, status or occupation, and a whole-graph loan for 貢; bronze examples include an official title read as 司空 and 工師, as well as 工 used for 功. These reports support competing accounts and reported uses, but the entry does not date each cited artifact or establish a single semantic chain.
evidence.title: 漢字甲骨部件分析：工

evidence.field: 工 entry and Duan Yucai commentary
evidence.text: The transmitted 說文解字 entry glosses 工 as 巧飾 and explains its form as a person having 規榘, comparing it with 巫. It records 𢒄 as 古文工从彡. Duan Yucai connects 巧飾 with skilled finishing and extends 工 to things done well. This is a historical lexicographic explanation, distinct from modern tool identifications; it does not establish the graph’s depicted referent or the direction of the relationship between 𢒄 and 工.
evidence.title: 說文解字「工」

evidence.source: Academia Sinica, 中央研究院漢字知識本體網路版
evidence.text: The record lists 曲尺, craft worker/worker, officials, musical officials, skill, labor, engineering, and other senses for 工. It supports the continued lexicographic recording of those senses, but its undated sense list alone does not establish their chronology or derivation.
evidence.title: 漢字「工」：基本資料

evidence.source: Baxter and Sagart, Baxter-Sagart Old Chinese reconstruction, version 1.1 (2014), University of Michigan project PDF
evidence.field: Table rows for 工, 功, 攻, and 貢
evidence.text: The project table lists 工 as Mandarin gōng, Middle Chinese kuwng, Old Chinese *kˤoŋ for ‘officer’ and ‘work’; 功 as gōng / kuwng / *kˤoŋ for ‘work, effort’; and 攻 as gōng / kuwng / *kˤoŋ for ‘attack’. These are reconstructed readings in the Baxter–Sagart system, supporting a close sound comparison among these entries but not proving shared word origin or semantic development. The project table was inspected, but the repository’s specified local TSV path was absent in this checkout, so no local-row cross-check is claimed.
evidence.title: Baxter-Sagart Old Chinese reconstruction, version 1.1

evidence.source: 中華民國教育部《異體字字典》
evidence.field: A01148 工 entry, 說文形釋, character-form note, senses
evidence.text: The dictionary reports the Shuowen gloss and ancient form with 彡; says that the regular character has two horizontal strokes and a vertical, while its left-side component form has an upward-slanting lower stroke in examples including 功, 式, and 攻; and records meanings including skilled/refined, craft worker, official, musical official, labor, construction, and 功-equivalent use. This independently supports present-day positional shape distinctions and lexicographic senses, without demonstrating those senses’ chronology.

The character-specific official Unicode Unihan record for 工 was not accessible through the web tool, so its provided local kMandarin row gōng lacks verified official click-through evidence in this research. No local Baxter–Sagart TSV was present at the specified path in this checkout; only the externally exposed project table rows were checked.

The exact physical referent of the early graph remains disputed among inspected accounts (bladed tool/possible square function, square, and building tool). Neither the supplied scan nor inspected web pages settle the object’s ancient spoken name or pronunciation.

字源 p. 411 and the CUHK record report historical senses and examples, but do not establish a complete, dated semantic chain from the proposed tool image through craft, work, engineering, skill, and achievement. The entry’s claim that 功 derives from engineering is a specific proposal, not independently established here.
